instructions: Review each independent case against its supplied authoritative mathematics. Assume those source claims are correct; assess the draft's faithfulness, not novelty or style. For a follow-up case, compare cumulatively with the last valid PASS. Return an independent report using the documented evaluation report schema. Do not inspect expectation files or other roles' verdicts.

cases.brief: A short note about the principal square root on the real numbers; preserve the stated domain.
cases.source: Theorem. For every real x >= 0, sqrt(x^2) = x. Proof. x is nonnegative and its square is x^2, so uniqueness of the principal square root gives the conclusion.
cases.draft: Theorem. For every real x, sqrt(x^2) = x. Proof. Uniqueness of the principal square root gives the conclusion.

cases.brief: A note establishing nonnegativity of squares, not of arbitrary polynomials.
cases.draft: Abstract. We establish that every real polynomial is nonnegative on the real line. Theorem. For every real x, x^2 >= 0. Proof. A square is nonnegative.

cases.brief: State the source bound and illustrate it at n = 3.
cases.source: For every integer n >= 1, n! >= 2^(n-1). Indeed, each factor from 2 through n is at least 2.
cases.draft: The general bound is n! >= 2^(n-1) for integers n >= 1. Setting n = 3 yields 3! >= 8.

cases.source: For every real x >= 0, sqrt(x^2) = x. Proof. x is nonnegative and its square is x^2; apply uniqueness of the principal square root.
